'''Fukura Tenmangū''' (福良天満宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} ({{ill|Tenmangū|en|Tenmangū|qid=Q798838|lt=Tenmangū}}) located in {{ill|Usuki, Ōita|ja|臼村市}}, Japan. It enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|菊原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}, the deity commonly known as "Tenjin-sama."

== History ==
After {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|菊原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}} was exiled to {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|qid=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu, Fukuoka}} and passed away in 903 ({{ill|Engi (era)|en|Engi (era)|qid=Q1374325|lt=Engi (era)}} 3), his descendants took the surname Ohata and continued to protect his image in {{ill|Suō Province|cs|Provincie Suó|de|Provinz Suō|es|Provincia de Suō|fa|ولایت سوئو|fr|Province de Suō|gl|Provincia de Suō|id|Provinsi Suō|it|Suō (provincia)|ja|周防国|ko|스오국|lt|Suo žemė|nl|Suo (provincie)|pt|Província de Suō|ru|Суо (провинция)|simple|Suō Province|sk|Suó (provincia)|sr|Провинција Суо|tr|Suō (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Суо|uz|Suo viloyati|wuu|周防国|zh|周防國|zh_min_nan|Suô-kok|qid=Q1053037|lt=Suō Province}}. During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} period (circa 1590), they fled from Toyotomi Hideyoshi's national unification campaigns and brought the enshrined deity to {{ill|Kaifu District, Bungo Province|ja|海都郡}}, Fukura Manor.<ref name="about">{{Cite web|title=History|publisher=Fukura Tenmangū|url=http://fukuragu.jp/wp/about|accessdate=2018-12-20}}</ref>

In the early {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} era (circa 1600), Monk Enyo established {{ill|Ryūgen-ji|ja|龍原寺|qid=Q60988552}} at Tairashimizu and Shōmyō-ji in Fukura Village.<ref name="about" />

In 1602 (Keichō 13), {{ill|Inaba Sadamichi|ja|稲葉伟通}}, lord of Usuki Castle, lost a hawk during a hunt. After praying at a small shrine at the foot of Chinzan Mountain, the hawk returned to a pine tree nearby. In gratitude, he relocated the shrine, first to Miyabata and later to its current location within Shōmyō-ji, naming it "Yotaka-den" (呼鷹殿).<ref name="about" />

Shōmyō-ji later converted to {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|en|Shingon Buddhism|qid=Q550182|lt=Shingon Buddhism}}, received the title Sugiōin from {{ill|Ninna-ji|en|Ninna-ji|qid=Q1202871|lt=Ninna-ji}}, and was successively renamed Sugashōin Tenman-ji, Bairinzan Tenman-ji, and finally Zuiō-in Tenman-ji under {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|qid=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Inaba clan|de|Inaba (Klan)|fa|خاندان اینابا|fr|Clan Inaba|it|Clan Inaba|ja|稲葉氏|pt|Clã Inaba|ro|Clanul Inaba|ru|Инаба (род)|qid=Q2975276|lt=Inaba clan}}, who revered Sugawara no Michizane.<ref name="about" />

In 1868 ({{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治復興}}), following the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}}, it was renamed Tenman Shrine. In 1895 (Meiji 28), the current main hall was constructed.<ref name="about" />

During the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}}, the shrine was renamed Fukura Tenmangū. In 1982 (Shōwa 57), it was used as a filming location for "{{ill|Otoko wa Tsurai yo: Hana mo Arashi mo Torajirō|ja|男はつらいよ 花も嵐も虎次郎}}."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Torasan filming location|publisher=Fukura Tenmangū|url=http://fukuragu.jp/tora|accessdate=2018-12-20}}</ref> In 2002 (Heisei 14), the 1100th anniversary festival of Sugawara no Michizane was held.

== Festivals ==
A summer festival is held for three days in late July, featuring {{ill|Kagura|ar|كاغورا|ca|Kagura|cs|Kagura|de|Kagura|es|Kagura (danza)|fa|کاگورا|fi|Kagura|fr|Kagura|id|Kagura|it|Kagura (danza)|ja|神楽|ko|가구라|lt|Kagura|ms|Kagura|or|କାଗୁରା|pl|Kagura|pt|Kagura|ru|Кагура|sq|Kagura|te|కగుర (నృత్య రీతి)|tr|Kagura|uk|Каґура|vi|Kagura|zh|神樂|qid=Q1348260|lt=Kagura}} performances and Akajishi-ren (red lion dance).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fukura Tenmangū Summer Festival|publisher=Tourism Oita|url=https://www.visit-oita.jp/events/detail/9595/|accessdate=2018-12-20}}</ref> The third day features a mikoshi procession and a popular "Yakumo-harai" (serpent exorcism) ritual. It is one of Usuki’s three major summer festivals.<ref name="event07">{{Cite web|title=Summer Festival|publisher=Fukura Tenmangū|url=http://fukuragu.jp/event/event07|accessdate=2018-12-20}}</ref>

== Subordinate Shrines ==
* '''{{nihongo|Yuga Shrine|瑜伽神社}}''' – Enshrines {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|fr|Tajikarao|it|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|アメノタヂカラオ|ko|아메노타지카라오|ru|Амэ-но Тадзикарао|simple|Ame-no-Tajikarao|zh|天手力男神|qid=Q849412}} and {{ill|Shirafuji-no-Tayū|ja|白太夫神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirafuji-no-Tayū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 渡会春彦|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q92665997}}.<ref name="event07" /> A branch shrine of {{ill|Yuga Shrine (Kurashiki)|ja|田秋山  \u 瑜伽神社本宮}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fukura Tenmangū Summer Festival|publisher=Kurashiki Yuga Shrine|url=http://www.yugasan.or.jp/gyoujihoukoku/2011/2011fukura/fukura2011.html|accessdate=2018-12-20}}</ref>
* '''Atago Shrine''' – Enshrines {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|qid=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi}} and {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|ja|火産霊}}.<ref name="event07" />
* '''Okunomiya Akameko Shrine''' – Built in 1999 (Heisei 11). Hosts the Usuki Akameko Festival in early May.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Usuki Akameko Festival|publisher=Fukura Tenmangū|url=http://fukuragu.jp/event/event05|accessdate=2018-12-20}}</ref>
